readings: Consider patients who have at least one single laboratory record in which `U-PRO` is exactly '-' AND `RA` is exactly '-' (both on the same record). For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records (not only the qualifying ones) to compute the average `PT` and the average of the row-wise difference `TAT` − `TAT2`, ignoring NULLs (the difference is taken only on records where both `TAT` and `TAT2` are non-null). Return one row with the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages, unrounded.

Consider patients who have at least one laboratory record with `U-PRO` exactly '-' and also at least one laboratory record (the same or a different one) with `RA` exactly '-', so the two results may come from different records. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average `PT` and the average of the row-wise difference `TAT` − `TAT2`, ignoring NULLs (the difference is taken only on records where both `TAT` and `TAT2` are non-null). Return one row with the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages, unrounded.
queries:
SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_tat_diff
FROM (
    SELECT ID,
           AVG(PT) AS avg_pt,
           AVG(CASE WHEN TAT IS NOT NULL AND TAT2 IS NOT NULL THEN TAT - TAT2 END) AS avg_diff
    FROM Laboratory
    WHERE ID IN (
        SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'
    )
    GROUP BY ID
);
SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_tat_diff
FROM (
    SELECT ID,
           AVG(PT) AS avg_pt,
           AVG(CASE WHEN TAT IS NOT NULL AND TAT2 IS NOT NULL THEN TAT - TAT2 END) AS avg_diff
    FROM Laboratory
    WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-')
      AND ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA = '-')
    GROUP BY ID
);
